title: He offered his daughters… to protect his reputation.
paragraphs: He offered his daughters… to protect his reputation.

Not a villain.
Not a pagan king.
A man the Bible still calls “righteous.”
And here’s the tension you can’t escape:
How does a “righteous” man make a decision that dark?

How do you stand for God…
and still think like the world?
What if we’re not as different from Lot as we think?
But the Bible gives us honest ones.
“Look, I have two daughters who have never slept with a man. Let me bring them out to you…” — Genesis 19:8
We want to explain it away.
Because this isn’t just about Lot.
This is about what happens when you live close enough to sin… that it starts to feel normal.
Lot didn’t wake up that day planning to say those words.
you say yes to something you would’ve once rebuked.
And here’s the truth that cuts deep:
You don’t fall in the moment.
In the things you told yourself were “not that bad.”
Lot chose Sodom long before Sodom shaped him.
“Lot chose for himself the whole plain of the Jordan… and pitched his tents near Sodom.” — Genesis 13:11–12
📖 SCRIPTURE ANCHOR — WHAT GOD IS REALLY SHOWING US
“…and if He rescued righteous Lot, greatly distressed by the sensual conduct of the wicked…” — 2 Peter 2:7
Some scholars interpret this as meaning Lot’s heart was still aligned with God—
but his life choices placed him in environments that corrupted his judgment.
Because righteousness is not just what you believe.
It’s what shapes your decisions under pressure.
You can be saved… and still be spiritually weakened.
You can belong to God… and still think like Sodom.
⚡ THE GOSPEL TURN — WHERE LOT FAILED, JESUS STOOD
Because this is where everything shifts.
Let that collide in your spirit.
Where Lot stood at a door, negotiating with evil—
“He was pierced for our transgressions… crushed for our iniquities.” — Isaiah 53:5
“God made Him who knew no sin to be sin for us…” — 2 Corinthians 5:21

Lot tried to sacrifice innocence
to protect what he valued.

Jesus became the sacrifice
to redeem what we destroyed.
And here’s the scandal of grace:
“When he lingered, the men seized him… the LORD being merciful to him.” — Genesis 19:16
He had to be dragged out.
Even if your decisions don’t match your confession…
Even if you’ve lingered longer than you should have—
💔 RESOLUTION — THIS IS WHERE IT GETS PERSONAL
So now the question is not about Lot.
What are you living “near” right now?
that is slowly teaching your soul to negotiate with sin?
Sodom doesn’t need to enter your life fully to destroy you.
will speak louder than what you claim to believe.

Jesus doesn’t just expose compromise.
He rescues compromised people.
✝️ INVITATION — COME OUT BEFORE IT BURNS
Come out of what’s shaping you wrong.
Come out of what’s dulling your conviction.
Come out of what’s rewriting your standards.
Because grace is not permission to stay.
He’s not waiting to condemn you.
